key_insight: Accurately approximating the score function in a diffusion model can be converted into a quantitative guarantee that the generated distribution is close to the target data distribution in KL divergence, with an added term for terminal prior mismatch.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a theoretical bridge from neural network approximation quality to end-to-end generative fidelity, helping guide model capacity, noise schedules, and reverse-process initialization.
method: Use Hornik-style universal approximation to relate neural networks to score-function approximation.
Apply Girsanov's theorem on path space to bound divergence between reverse diffusion trajectories.
Use the data processing inequality for relative entropy to transfer path-space error into distribution-level KL bounds.
evidence_signal: The paper is theoretical and derives an explicit upper bound from approximation theory; the abstract does not report experiments or numerical evaluation.
watch_item: The guarantee still depends on the mismatch between the forward diffusion terminal distribution and the chosen reverse-process prior, so poor prior initialization can limit performance even with accurate score approximation.
paper_title: From Score Approximation to Distribution Approximation in Score-Based Diffusion Models
